sources.citation: van den Bel, Martijn & Mariana Françozo (eds.). 2023. The Tapuia of Northeastern Brazil in Dutch Sources (1628–1648). Leiden/Boston: Brill. xvi+275 pp. e-ISBN 978-90-04-54364-5; DOI 10.1163/9789004543645. Open access (CC BY-NC-ND 4.0).
sources.note: No phonology content. The 'Note on Transcription and Translation' (pp. 18-19) concerns Dutch paleography ('mixed method'; original spellings of foreign names and words kept unharmonized); the Glossary (p. 277) lists colonial Dutch/Portuguese/French/Tupi terms (aldeia, farinha, mandioca, Taponiers..), not Tarairiu words; the Introduction states the Tapuia 'were not a distinct Indigenous group and did not speak similar languages'; Arciszewski's account notes the interpreters could not follow the Tapuia language. Indigenous words occur only embedded in the documents (names, 'Kou-wou' etc.) with…

sources.citation: Santos, Juvandi de Souza. 2009. Cariri e Tarairiú? Culturas tapuias nos sertões da Paraíba. Tese (Doutorado em História), Pontifícia Universidade Católica do Rio Grande do Sul, Porto Alegre.
sources.note: Largest modern compilation of Tarairiú lexical/toponymic items (source of the Wikipedia/Wiktionary lists); would confirm that no phonological notes exist. History thesis, so a stress statement is very unlikely.

sources.citation: Teensma, B. N. 2000. O diário de Rodolfo Baro (1647) como monumento aos índios Tarairiú do Rio Grande do Norte. In: Almeida, Luiz Sávio de; Galindo, Marcos; Elias, Juliana Lopes (orgs.), Índios do Nordeste: temas e problemas 2, pp. 81-99. Maceió: EDUFAL.
sources.note: Nothing on stress, accent or tone (a full-text search for stress/accent acento|tônica|sílaba|pronúncia|fonolog|fonét: no hits). Language content is philological and negative: p. 86 calls the Tarairiú speech 'um idioma incompreensível da família linguística Jê' (aside); pp. 87-88 reject Moreau's claim that Baro spoke Tarairiú and state 'a terminologia índia no seu Diário de 1647 é exclusivamente tupi'; p. 90 and fn. 20 (p. 99) show that several items in the printed 'Tarairiu' record are misreadings — corpamba < (ipe)cacuanha, Houcha < taoeba/Taúba, and Barlaeus' 'Titzsheynos' and 'Kehnturah' <…

sources.citation: Medeiros Filho, Olavo de. 1999. Os Tarairiús, extintos tapuias do Nordeste. In: Almeida, L. S. de; Galindo, M; Silva, E. (orgs.), Índios do Nordeste: temas e problemas, pp. 241-257. Maceió: EDUFAL.
sources.note: Nothing. pp.251-252 'Linguagem dos Tarairiús': 'O idioma dos tapuias tarairiús.. infelizmente não foi preservado. Assim, não dispomos de informações sobre o léxico daqueles tarairiús'; lists 6 terms gleaned from Dutch chroniclers (carfa, corpamba, corraveara, manuah, oiugi, uva) and a 14-word Tarairiú/Jê/Cariri comparison supplied by J. E. Barbosa Borges. No phonology of any kind.

sources.note: Nothing. 'Tarairiú or Ochucuyana - extinct language once spoken between the Assú and Apodí Rivers.. [Marcgravi de Liebstad 1648; Schuller 1912, pp. 89-98.]'; comparative table gives only agh 'sun', kén 'stone', ake 'tobacco'.

sources.citation: Pompeu Sobrinho, Thomaz. 1958. Línguas tapuias desconhecidas do Nordeste: alguns vocabulários inéditos. Boletim de Antropologia (Instituto de Antropologia, Universidade do Ceará, Fortaleza) ano 2, vol. 1: 3-19.
sources.note: Nothing for Tarairiu: pp. 5-8 state that after 'exaustivas comparações' (1935) the author concluded 'os tarairiú falavam uma língua independente ou isolada', rejects Schuller's Carib affinity, and lists the tribes he assigns to the family; no Tarairiu words, no transcription or prosody remarks. sources.citation: Loukotka, Čestmír. 1955. Les langues non-Tupí du Brésil du Nord-Est. In: Herbert Baldus (ed.), Anais do XXXI Congresso Internacional de Americanistas (São Paulo, 1954), vol. II, pp. 1029-1054. São Paulo: Editora Anhembi.
sources.note: Nothing; ethnohistorical/classificatory survey. States the entire corpus is Schuller's 26 words + 20 names and classes the language as isolated. No wordlist printed for Tarairiuw here, no phonology.

sources.citation: Pinto, Estevão. 1935. Os indígenas do Nordeste, 1.º tomo. (Brasiliana 44.) São Paulo: Companhia Editora Nacional.
sources.note: Ethnographic classification survey; groups the Tarairiús with 'tapuias' after Ehrenreich; no linguistic data, nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Pinto, Estevão. 1935. Os indígenas do Nordeste. 1.º tomo (Biblioteca Pedagógica Brasileira, série V, Brasiliana, vol. 44). São Paulo: Companhia Editora Nacional.
sources.note: Nothing. The Tarairiu appear in a two-sentence classificatory note (placed among the Gê, following Ehrenreich) and the Janduí of Açu/Apodi in a list of Cariri-group tribes; the volume's language chapter concerns Tupi/língua geral and general classification, with no Tarairiu words, transcription or phonology.

sources.citation: Pompeu Sobrinho, Thomaz. 1934. Os Tapuias do Nordeste e a monografia de Elias Herckman. Revista do Instituto do Ceará 48: 7-28. Fortaleza.
sources.note: Nothing. Ethnographic commentary (physical type, houses, food, war, marriage, funerary endocannibalism, shamans) on Herckman; the only language content is ethnonyms/chiefs' names and a remark on the '48 diferentes maneiras de grafar uma mesma palavra indígena'. No wordlist, no phonology.

sources.note: The only linguistic treatment Loukotka cites for Tarairiú (pp. 89-98); assembles the 17th-century word scraps from Marcgrav/Theatrum; would be the place any remark on the transcriptions lives, though a stress rule is not expected.
